abstract: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) is an inborn error of metabolism caused by mutations in the mitochondrial branched-chain -keto acid dehydrogenase (BCKDH) complex, resulting in toxic accumulation of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) and their corresponding branched-chain keto acids (BCKAs). This leads to poorly understood clinical features in both brain and muscle. Due to a limited understanding of MSUD pathophysiology, there is a marked paucity of effective pharmacological interventions. Here, we discovered the mTOR inhibitor, rapamycin, improves disease and extends survival in MSUD mouse models. Rapamycin treatment attenuates neuroinflammation and reduces muscle pathology. To investigate the mechanism behind these effects, we studied the accumulation of BCAAs and BCKAs. Rapamycin decreased BCAA accumulation. Overall, our work identifies rapamycin as a potential therapy for MSUD. More broadly, it suggests dysregulated mTOR signaling may drive MSUD pathobiology and advances our understanding of the mechanisms influencing leucine toxicity.
